title: The moat illusion – China’s bid to deflate US AI valuations
gist: Oxford Economics argues the global AI order is splitting into two competing systems — a US-led 'Pax Silica' built on trusted chips and compute and a China-led 'WAICO' built on cheap, open models — and that China is running its classic overcapacity playbook in AI. Because models cross borders digitally at zero marginal cost, the deflationary hit could exceed prior manufacturing cycles and compress US hyperscaler valuations, with the US moat eroding fast at the model layer while holding at compute.

insights.claim: The global AI order is forming as two partly competing governance and distribution systems rather than converging on a single winner: a US-led bloc organised around access to trusted chips, compute and tech supply chains, and a China-led bloc offering lower-cost, more open models and AI capacity-building.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Model the AI trade as two distribution stacks with different customers rather than one winner-take-all market; exposure to chip/compute chokepoints and exposure to model pricing are separate risk factors.
insights.quote: the US-led Pax Silica is built around access to trusted chips, compute, and tech supply chains, while the China-led WAICO is premised on a broader offer of lower-cost, more open models and AI capacity-building.
insights.locator: The global AI order is taking shape

themes.theme: China's overcapacity playbook applied to AI

insights.claim: China is applying to AI models the same overcapacity playbook it previously ran in infrastructure, housing, solar panels and electric vehicles.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Expect the same margin destruction pattern seen in solar and EVs to show up in AI model pricing — price, not capability, is the attack vector.
insights.quote: China is running its familiar overcapacity playbook on its AI models, just like infrastructure, housing, solar panels or electric vehicles before.
insights.locator: China is running its familiar overcapacity

insights.claim: Because AI models cross borders digitally at zero marginal cost, the competitive impact of China's AI build-out could be considerably larger than that of prior manufacturing overcapacity cycles.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Tariffs and physical trade barriers that blunted past Chinese overcapacity waves are far weaker defences here; the deflation can arrive faster and reach further into Western software pricing.
insights.quote: Because AI models cross borders digitally at zero marginal cost, the competitive impact of China’s AI build-out could be considerably larger than prior manufacturing cycles.
insights.locator: Because AI models cross borders digitally

insights.claim: Low-cost Chinese AI models are narrowing the US AI advantage, reshaping competition and raising questions over valuations, compute demand and the economics of AI scale.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: The core investment question shifts from who has the best model to whether AI scale economics still justify current US AI valuations.
insights.locator: China’s low-cost AI models are narrowing

themes.theme: Where the US moat erodes and where it holds

insights.claim: The US AI moat is shrinking unevenly: it is compressing quickly at the model layer while holding up reasonably well at the compute layer.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Favour the compute/infrastructure layer over model-layer businesses when pricing durable competitive advantage in US AI.
insights.quote: The US AI moat is shrinking unevenly as it quickly compresses at the model layer, holds up reasonably well at compute
insights.locator: The US AI moat is shrinking unevenly

insights.claim: The US AI advantage is increasingly taxed at home by state-level power and permitting friction.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Watch US state-level electricity and permitting policy as a domestic drag on AI capacity build-outs — a cost input that can erode the compute moat from within.
insights.quote: increasingly taxed at home by state-level power and permitting friction
insights.locator: The US AI moat is shrinking unevenly

insights.claim: China's low-cost AI push is assessed specifically for what it could mean for hyperscaler valuations, framing the analysis around where US advantages are eroding versus where they remain resilient.
insights.speaker: Sally Li
insights.so_what: Hyperscaler multiples are the explicit transmission channel from Chinese AI price competition to portfolio returns.
insights.quote: We assess where US advantages are eroding, where they remain resilient and what China’s low-cost AI push could mean for hyperscaler valuations.
insights.locator: Can the US AI moat hold?
